memories.content: The user's maternal aunt keeps one spare key to the user's home.
If the door is locked, the user is accustomed to contacting their maternal aunt, who has the spare key, before contacting building management.
When going to collect the spare key from their maternal aunt, the user wants to give an arrival time first so neither person has to wait.
The user feels at ease only after returning a borrowed spare key in person on the same day.
The user feels uneasy about writing down a new entrance passcode on paper.
The user found it difficult when a family member arrived without notice during a meeting and the user could not respond immediately.
On a day their younger brother received a package for them, the user felt reassured after checking the delivery photo.
The user's maternal aunt wants confirmation that the user is coming in person before handing over the spare key.
Confirm with the user before sharing the spare key's storage location or the maternal aunt's contact information.
The management office of a multi-unit residential building does not hold a unit key without verifying identity.
The user stores prepared meals on the second shelf of the freezer.
The user went to the market without a shopping list and bought onions that were already at home.
On a day the user shopped after checking a refrigerator photo, they did not make a duplicate purchase.
On a day the user made a spicy stew, they left part of one bowl uneaten.
The next time the user cooked it, they used half as much chili powder and finished the meal.
When cooking with their younger brother, the user assigned the cooking sequence only verbally and they did the same task twice.
The next time, the user and their younger brother split ingredient preparation and heat control and finished the meal 20 minutes earlier.
When cooking together, the user's younger brother prefers to divide the cooking and dishwashing roles in advance.
The local agent can compare responses across several meals, but it cannot conclude from one unfinished food item that the user dislikes that ingredient.
The condition of frozen prepared food may vary with its packaging and storage duration.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate practical domains: the reference centers on home access, privacy, and family coordination, while the compared frame centers on food storage, shopping, cooking, and cautious inference. No claims govern the same operational decision, and no conflict or scope-dependent difference appears.
